message.content:
**Uno – Quick Overview** | Item | Details | |------|---------| | **Deck** | 108 cards: 4 colors (Red, Yellow, Green, Blue) × 25 cards each (one 0, two 1‑9, two “Draw Two”, two “Skip”, two “Reverse”), plus 4 “Wild” and 4 “Wild Draw Four”. | | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or a pre‑agreed total). Points are tallied after each round. | | **Setup** | • Deal 7 cards to each player.
• Place the remaining deck face down as the draw pile.
• Flip the top card to start the discard pile; if it’s an action card, apply its effect immediately. | | **Turn Order** | Players take turns clockwise (unless a “Reverse” changes direction). | | **Playing a Card** | On your turn you may play one card that matches either the color or the value of the top discard.
• If you play a “Wild” or “Wild Draw Four”, you choose the new color. | | **Action Cards** | • **Draw Two** – Next player draws 2 cards and loses their turn.
• **Skip** – Next player loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – Reverses play direction.
• **Wild** – You choose the next color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – Same as Wild, but next player draws 4 cards and loses their turn. | | **Drawing** | If you cannot play a card, you must draw from the draw pile until you get a playable card. If you still can’t play, your turn ends. | | **Calling “Uno”** | When you have only one card left, shout “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn. If you forget and another player catches you, you must draw two penalty cards. | | **Winning a Round** | The round ends when a player discards all their cards. That player scores points equal to the sum of the values of all cards remaining in opponents’ hands (number cards = face value, Draw Two/Skip/Reverse = 20, Wild/Wild Draw Four = 50). | | **Scoring** | Add round points to the winner’s total. Play continues until someone reaches the target score. | **Optional Variations** | Variation | Effect | |-----------|--------| | **Stacking** | Players may stack “Draw Two” or “Wild Draw Four” cards on top of each other, forcing the next player to draw the cumulative total unless they can stack further. | | **No Wild Draw Four Challenge** | Some groups allow players to challenge a “Wild Draw Four” if they suspect the previous player had a playable card; if the challenge fails, the challenger draws 4 cards. | | **Custom Decks** | Use themed decks or add extra cards for house rules. | That’s the core of Uno—simple to learn, fast to play, and full of strategy and luck!
